citing_name: Davis Wright & Jones v. National Union Fire Insurance
citing_court: United States District Court for the Western District of Washington
cited_court: Supreme Court of the United States
negated_by: Thomas v. Washington Gas Light Co.
proposition: Full faith and credit bars relitigating in a second state a claim already adjudicated under another state's law.
reason: Court calls the Magnolia principle fully applicable; Thomas declared Magnolia should be overruled on that very preclusion holding; no acknowledgment.

citing_name: International Ass'n of Machinists v. Sandsberry
cited_court: Supreme Court of the United States
proposition: Action by a private association is not governmental action subject to constitutional restraints.
reason: Smith v. Allwright overruled Grovey's holding that party exclusion was not state action; the court cites Grovey for no governmental action without notice.

citing_name: In re Fedex Ground Package System, Inc., Employment Practices Litigati
citing_court: United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana
cited_name: Wilkinson v. Palmetto State Transp. Co.
negated_by: Wilkinson v. Palmetto State Transportation Co.
proposition: Employee versus independent contractor turns on right to control; four factors determine the right of control.
reason: Court of appeals decision reversed as a whole on the employee/independent contractor test and its application; cited as authority with no subsequent history.

citing_name: Holler v. Hartford Life & Accident Insurance
citing_court: United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio
cited_court: United States District Court for the District of Minnesota
proposition: Arbitrary and capricious to require objective evidence for a fibromyalgia claim where the plan does not require it.
reason: Eighth Circuit reversed, holding it was not unreasonable to require clinical documentation; cited as support with no subsequent history.

cited_name: National League of Cities v. Usery
cited_court: Supreme Court of the United States
negated_by: Garcia v. San Antonio Metropolitan Transit Authority
proposition: Tenth Amendment limits Congress's power to override state sovereignty even when exercising its commerce power.
reason: Garcia overruled National League of Cities entirely on this Tenth Amendment limit; court states it as governing law without noting that.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cited_name: Public Citizen Health Research Group v. Department of Health, Educatio
cited_court: United States District Court for the District of Columbia
negated_by: Public Citizen Health Research Group, v. Department of Healt
proposition: A PSRO with legal authority to make conclusive benefit determinations is an agency.
reason: Used as a benchmark holding for agency status; the D.C. Circuit reversed precisely because the PSRO is not an agency; no acknowledgment.

proposition: Jury trial waiver cannot rest on scheduling practice absent the defendant's deliberate election to forgo a jury.
reason: Virginia Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals on exactly the jury trial request holding; cited as supporting authority with no subsequent history.

citing_court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
negated_by: Neuhoff Bros. Packers Management Corp. v. Wilson
proposition: Whether conduct qualifies as dishonest is more often than not a question best resolved by a jury.
reason: Texas Supreme Court reversed the judgment resting on the jury's no-dishonesty finding; no subsequent history noted by citing court.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York
negated_by: Life Insurance Co. of Georgia v. Smith
proposition: Punitive damages are available without a compensatory award so long as plaintiff suffered some injury.
reason: Life of Georgia overruled Caterpillar to the extent it allowed punitive damages without compensatory or nominal award; cited without acknowledgment.

proposition: A jurisdiction recognizes a common-law action for serving liquor to a known alcoholic through intentional or reckless misconduct.
reason: Jackson overruled Grasser's recognition of that very cause of action; cited as supporting authority without history.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
negated_by: Womble ex rel. Havard v. Singing River Hospital
proposition: Public-service physicians have qualified immunity for medical treatment decisions unless they commit willful wrongs or malicious acts.
reason: Womble overruled Hudson to exactly that extent; court applies the rule via Sparks quoting Hudson without noting Womble.

citing_name: Miller v. International Diving & Consulting Services, Inc.
cited_name: Holmes v. J. Ray McDermott & Co.
cited_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
proposition: Punitive damages for failure to pay maintenance and cure lie where conduct is callous, willful, arbitrary.
reason: Guevara overruled Holmes's holding that such punitive damages are available; citing court applies that standard without noting it.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
cited_court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
proposition: A parolee continues serving his sentence during parole; the sentence is neither abated nor suspended.
reason: Parker disapproved Gantt without limitation, and Gantt's reasoning that parolees still serve their term outside is what is taken; no acknowledgment.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Southern District of New York
cited_court: United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois
proposition: A scheme aimed at tangible property (money) rather than intangible rights states mail or wire fraud; Regan distinguished.
reason: Seventh Circuit reversed the district court's refusal to dismiss on mail fraud sufficiency; cited as support with no subsequent history.

proposition: Defendant's failure to present evidence or request an instruction at trial is fatal to his later claim of error.
reason: Court of Appeals decision applying procedural default was reversed and dismissed by Supreme Court, which reached the unpreserved errors; no acknowledgment.

citing_name: Johnson v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance
citing_court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
proposition: 'Use' of a vehicle includes a child's accidental asphyxiation from the mother's suicide by exhaust.
reason: Minnesota Supreme Court reversed that very holding, rejecting the court of appeals' use test; West Virginia court cites it without the reversal.

proposition: On review of a contested case the court examines the record for substantial evidence.
reason: Cited as authority for the substantial evidence review; the decision was reversed as a whole for misapplying that very standard, with no acknowledgment.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee
proposition: Illinois exempts negligent tenants from landlord's insurer's subrogation; insurance presumed for mutual benefit.
reason: Geekie overruled Anderson on exactly this subrogation holding four months earlier; cited as current Illinois law without acknowledgment.

cited_court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
proposition: Laboratory test report is admissible under a hearsay exception without the testing chemist or technician testifying.
reason: Matulewicz disapproved Malsbury on exactly this point; cited as supporting authority with no subsequent history.

citing_name: Pelican Homestead & Savings Ass'n v. Winston
cited_name: League Central Credit Union v. Montgomery
negated_by: First Guaranty Bank v. Baton Rouge Petroleum Center, Inc.
proposition: Any defense that could defeat executory proceedings may be urged to bar a later deficiency judgment suit.
reason: First Guaranty overruled League Central on exactly this rule two weeks earlier; applied here without acknowledgment.

proposition: Severance for antagonistic defenses requires a defendant to face battling both the state and his co-defendant.
reason: Court of appeal decision was reversed in full by the Louisiana Supreme Court; cited by Cf. as authority with no subsequent history.

proposition: Prosecutor's remark that nobody contradicted a witness's testimony is permissible comment on the evidence, not on defendant's silence.
reason: Kinchen disapproved Bolton without limitation on its approach to comments on failure to testify, the same subject Dufour cites it for.

proposition: Circumstantial evidence test: whether a jury might reasonably find the evidence excluded every reasonable hypothesis except guilt.
reason: Alabama Supreme Court reversed the Court of Criminal Appeals' decision, which turned on circumstantial-evidence sufficiency; cited without subsequent history.

proposition: A judgment must be entered before an appeal is taken; it is not appealable until actually entered.
reason: Quotes division 2 of Gibson, the very holding Gillen overruled (premature appeal ineffective); applied to dismiss the appeal, no acknowledgment.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania
cited_name: Paschall v. Kansas City Star Co.
cited_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
negated_by: Paschall v. Kansas City Star Co.
proposition: Expense of expert research and testimony necessary to the litigation may be taxable costs.
reason: En banc court overruled the whole panel opinion and vacated the fee award; cited without that history as supporting authority.

citing_name: O'hara v. Board of Education of the Vocational School in the County of
citing_court: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey
cited_court: United States District Court for the District of South Carolina
proposition: Administrative hearing with full adjudicative procedures meets prerequisites for collateral estoppel in later federal civil rights suit.
reason: District decision giving preclusive effect to state administrative ruling was reversed outright on that very point; citing court relies without noting reversal.

citing_court: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cited_court: United States District Court for the Southern District of New York
proposition: Economic associations are within the First Amendment's protection of association.
reason: The district judgment resting on the First Amendment associational claim was reversed on appeal; cited as authority with no subsequent history.

citing_name: Western Idaho Production Credit Ass'n v. Simplot Feed Lots, Inc.
cited_name: Halperin v. Tri-State Livestock Credit Corp. (In re Ellsworth)
cited_court: United States Bankruptcy Appellate Panel for the Ninth Circuit
negated_by: Tri-State Livestock Credit Corp. v. Ellsworth
proposition: A secured party that authorizes disposition of collateral loses its security interest under UCC 9-306(2).
reason: Ninth Circuit reversed the BAP decision outright on the consent-to-sale issue; Idaho court cites it as authority without subsequent history.

citing_name: Young J. Lee, Inc. v. Commonwealth, Department of Revenue, Bureau of S
cited_court: United States District Court for the District of Montana
proposition: Government cannot revoke a permit a business depends on without sufficient due process; licenses create protected property interests.
reason: Ninth Circuit vacated the whole decision, holding no protected property interest and no claim; cited without that history.

proposition: A cause of action in negligence is the negligent act or acts which occasioned the injury.
reason: Superior Court decision was reversed as a whole on its cause-of-action ruling before this opinion; cited as accord noting only allocatur granted.

proposition: Informant reliability can be shown by independent verification, including a controlled buy, before the search.
reason: Arizona Supreme Court vacated the Court of Appeals opinion as a whole; citing court relies on it without noting that.

citing_name: Lasalle Extension University v. Federal Trade Commission
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
cited_name: Shermco Industries, Inc. v. Secretary of the United States Air Force
cited_court: United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas
negated_by: Shermco Industries, Inc. v. Secretary of Air Force
proposition: FOIA attorney fees may be awarded despite commercial self-interest where the agency asserted unreasonable exemption claims.
reason: Fifth Circuit reversed the whole judgment, upholding the exemptions and ordering judgment for the Air Force; no history noted.

citing_name: Schmid Laboratories v. Youngs Drug Products Corp.
citing_court: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey
cited_name: Scott Paper Co. v. Scott's Liquid Gold, Inc.
cited_court: United States District Court for the District of Delaware
negated_by: Scott Paper Co. v. Scott's Liquid Gold, Inc.
proposition: Purchasers of inexpensive goods are unlikely to exercise great care, a factor in likelihood-of-confusion analysis.
reason: Third Circuit reversed and vacated the whole judgment, including the district court's likelihood-of-confusion conclusion from which this factor is taken; no subsequent history noted.

citing_court: United States District Court for the District of Montana
cited_court: Supreme Court of the United States
proposition: The Tenth Amendment reserves purely local regulation to the states, limiting Congress's commerce power.
reason: Court invokes Hammer's reserved-powers reasoning to void a federal statute; Darby overruled Hammer's reasoning and conclusion without limitation; no acknowledgment.

cited_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
proposition: Allowing the jury to separate during deliberations is per se reversible error without showing prejudice.
reason: Arciniega overruled Panczko on exactly this point weeks earlier; Alaska court adopts the view without noting it.

citing_name: Charles N. Clark Associates, Ltd. v. Dependents of Robinson
proposition: Injury while travelling to an employer-directed medical appointment arises out of and in the course of employment.
reason: Arizona Supreme Court vacated the opinion and affirmed denial of compensation on that issue; cited as support without history.

negated_by: Piper v. Lockwood Water Users Ass'n
proposition: Customer of a contractor bears compensation insurance costs in the contract price, supporting treatment as having secured compensation.
reason: Piper overruled Fiscus in its entirety days earlier; cited as support for employer immunity reasoning without history.

proposition: An appeal taken from an oral pronouncement before entry of a written judgment presents nothing to review.
reason: Gillen overruled Benton's rule that a notice of appeal filed before entry of judgment is ineffective; Thomas applies that rule without noting it.

proposition: A burglary indictment or bill of information must specify the structure burglarized.
reason: James overruled McDonald outright for strictly construing indictments after verdict; Palmer cites it as authority for that indictment-specificity rule without noting the overruling.

proposition: Change of circumstances need not be shown to modify alimony or support fixed by consent judgment.
reason: Bernhardt overruled exactly this Moore holding as unsound; Catalano applies it months later without acknowledgment.

citing_name: Compton v. Paul K. Harding Realty Co.
proposition: Absence of a termination date does not render a shareholder agreement void.
reason: The appellate judgment was reversed as a whole by the Supreme Court with no limiting words shown; cited as authority without that history.

citing_name: Weidenhaft v. Shoppers Fair of Des Moines, Inc.
proposition: A storekeeper is not liable for a fall on a floor made slippery by tracked-in rain.
reason: Pribble overruled Gill's no-negligence holding for tracked-in water; the Iowa court lists Gill as supporting authority for directing a verdict, without notice.

cited_court: District Court of Appeal of the State of California
proposition: On resentencing after an invalid sentence, time served under the first sentence should be credited against the second.
reason: Fritz disapproved Silva's reasoning and conclusion on exactly this credit question; Idaho court cites it as supporting authority without noting that.

cited_name: Stark County Agricultural Society v. Brenner
negated_by: Meyer v. Cincinnati Street Ry. Co.
proposition: Joint tort liability lies where wrongdoers acted in concert and their want of care is of the same character.
reason: Meyer expressly overruled this third syllabus paragraph of Brenner; Logsdon states it as law without acknowledgment.

proposition: A clear statutory tax receipt is conclusive that prior taxes have been fully paid.
reason: The cited decision was set aside as a whole on rehearing, the court adopting the dissent; cited as authority with no subsequent history shown.

proposition: Operator who used ordinary care is not negligent for an unforeseeable equipment failure (spare wheel came off).
reason: Court of Civil Appeals judgment for the cab owner was reversed on the single question it decided; Utah court cites it without that history.

cited_court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
proposition: Facts a defendant could have explained or controverted but did not may be construed most strongly against him.
reason: Forte disapproved the statement at 114 App. Div. 517, the page cited, as conflicting with the no-presumption rule; no acknowledgment.

citing_name: First Nat. Bank in Hemphill v. Arnold
proposition: A fraudulent deed is not void and can be set aside only by suit within four years.
reason: Eckert v. Wendel expressly disapproved Gans on this point, holding a creditor need not sue in equity; cited as 'writ refused' only.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
proposition: Teacher killed travelling home with papers to grade suffered an injury arising out of and in the course of employment.
reason: Gintert overruled Inglish outright on exactly this compensability holding; D.C. Circuit cites it as supporting authority without noting the overruling.

citing_name: State ex rel. Barnett v. Gray
cited_name: State ex rel. Montgomery v. Anderson
negated_by: State ex rel. Allen v. Flaherty
proposition: A 30 per cent vote requirement for party nominations does not deny equal protection or discriminate.
reason: Montgomery's upholding of the 30 per cent provision is exactly what was overruled; citing court relies on it unacknowledged.

citing_name: Luce & Co., S. en C. v. Registrador de la Propiedad de Guayama
negated_by: State v. Inspiration Consolidated Copper Co.
proposition: No appeal lies from a decision in a special statutory proceeding unless a statute confers the right.
reason: Mohave's no-appeal holding in a special statutory proceeding is exactly what Inspiration overruled; cited as supporting authority without acknowledgment.

proposition: Recent possession of stolen property is not evidence of knowledge that it was stolen in a receiving charge.
reason: Guild overruled Bulla on exactly this point, holding recent possession raises the presumption for receiving too; Lardner cites Bulla as authority without notice.

proposition: It is mandatory that the jury declare the value of stolen property in its verdict; otherwise no jurisdiction to sentence.
reason: Griffith overruled Holmes without limitation on the value-finding requirement; Lee cites it as supporting authority with no mention of that.

proposition: Shown to the court means to make appear by proof; showing differs from merely stating.
reason: Lincoln overruled Cox, rejecting exactly its reading of 'shown ... by affidavit' as requiring more than making the affidavit.

citing_name: Northern Pac. Ry. Co. v. Crowell
citing_court: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey
negated_by: Globe Publishing Co. v. State Bank
proposition: Statute imposing personal liability on directors for failing to file reports is not penal.
reason: Globe Publishing overruled Howell's holding that such a statute is contractual not penal; cited as authority without acknowledgment.

proposition: Statutes making a liquor seller criminally liable for an employee's unauthorized sales are generally sustained.
reason: McCance overruled McGinnis's holding that the proprietor's contrary orders are no defense; cited as supporting authority without history.

proposition: Deceased's declarations of her own intention, not part of res gestae, are inadmissible hearsay when offered by the defendant.
reason: Trefethen overruled Felch on exactly this: such evidence should have been admitted to show the deceased's intention.

proposition: Statute giving justices jurisdiction of assault and battery, with 'except as otherwise provided', excludes that jurisdiction from circuit courts.
reason: Wilson overruled Ferguson's holding that circuit courts lacked original jurisdiction; the Nevada court quotes that very reasoning as support without noting the overruling.

proposition: A married woman's void contract or mere moral duty will not support her subsequent promise.
reason: Hixon v. Hetherington overruled the whole decision, holding her later note and mortgage enforceable; cited as settled doctrine without acknowledgment.
